_note: All English wording lives here. Plain text only — no <, > or & characters, because any data value inserted into these sentences is escaped by the build. Numbers must be written as {{stat:...}} tokens, never typed in, so a sentence can never drift away from the raw rows. Edit freely: py tools/build.py rebuilds every page.

Nothing here is estimated or invented: the charts, the sentences and the totals are all built from that file, and the file is empty. The target is {{stat:coverage.target}} observations.

home.lede: There is a queue here that everybody joins and nobody measures. This site is an attempt to measure it honestly: how long people really wait, where it is worst, and what the numbers still cannot tell us.
home.finding_place_median: At {{headline:place_name_en}}, half of the {{headline:n}} waits we timed were {{headline:median}} minutes or longer. That makes it the slowest place in this study.
home.rule_place_median: chosen because it has the highest median wait among the places with at least {{headline:min_n}} timed waits.
home.finding_share_over: {{headline:pct}} percent of the waits we timed ({{headline:over}} of {{headline:n}}) were longer than {{headline:threshold}} minutes. The longest was {{headline:minutes}} minutes at {{headline:place_name_en}} on {{headline:date}}.
home.rule_share_over: chosen because the share of long waits is the clearest signal in the data so far.
home.finding_longest_wait: The longest wait recorded so far was {{headline:minutes}} minutes at {{headline:place_name_en}} on {{headline:date}}.
home.rule_longest_wait: chosen because there are still too few timed waits to compare places by their median.
home.finding_no_timed: {{headline:logged}} observations are logged, but none of them has a recorded wait time yet, so there is no finding to show.
home.rule_no_timed: the site reports what is missing instead of guessing at it.
how_points: I stood in these queues myself with a watch, at different hours of the day, and wrote one row per wait into data/observations.csv.
Each row records the place, the date, the queue length and how long the person I followed waited. {{stat:coverage.collected}} rows exist so far, across {{stat:coverage.places_total}} known places.
Photos back up the rows that cite them, and the rows behind every chart are printed underneath it, so a reader can check any number against the file it came from.
home.flow_alt: How a raw row becomes a sentence on this page
home.flow_desc: A diagram in three steps: the raw comma-separated files that hold the rows I wrote by hand, then the generated file of computed figures, then the pages built from that file.
home.flow_node_1_sub: the rows I wrote by hand
home.flow_caption: Nothing on this site is typed in by hand. The raw files are the only source, so a chart cannot say something the file does not say.
home.no_photos: Photo evidence is still being collected. Nothing appears here until a photo exists together with its caption, its alt text and the place it was taken.
home.where_body: {{stat:coverage.places_with_data}} of the {{stat:coverage.places_total}} places in this study have observations so far, collected on {{stat:coverage.days_distinct}} days between {{stat:coverage.date_range}}. The places page draws each one at its position in the queue area.
home.ask_body: A field study only counts if somebody with the authority to change the queue reads it. The action page has a message you can copy, print or send exactly as it stands.

interview.title: The interview
interview.not_recorded: The interview has not been written up yet. It is published here only when the answers, the place and the person's permission are all recorded in data/interview.md.

data.lede: Every figure on this page is computed from data/observations.csv when the site is built. The site keeps no separate copy of any number.
data.empty_body: This page fills itself in as soon as rows are written into data/observations.csv. Until then it shows the collection target and nothing else: {{stat:coverage.collected}} of {{stat:coverage.target}} rows exist right now.
data.chart1_desc: A histogram of waiting times in fixed buckets. Bar height is the number of observations in each bucket, with the median marked by a dashed line.
data.chart1_finding: The waits cluster around the middle: the median is {{stat:wait.median}} minutes, the mean {{stat:wait.mean}} minutes, and the slowest {{stat:wait.max}} minutes. {{stat:wait.over_threshold}} of the {{stat:wait.count}} timed waits were longer than {{stat:wait.threshold}} minutes.
data.open_bucket_note: The last bar is open-ended: it holds every wait from that value upwards.
data.chart2_alt: Median waiting time at each place
data.chart2_desc: Horizontal bars showing the median waiting time at each place, with the value printed beside every bar.
data.chart2_finding: Comparing medians place by place is the fairest comparison here: the same counter can be quick in the morning and slow at midday, and a median keeps one bad hour from hiding behind a good day.
data.chart2_min_note: The paler bars are places with fewer than {{stat:min_place_n}} timed waits, so their medians are indicative only.
data.chart3_alt: Running total of minutes spent waiting
data.chart3_desc: A line showing the running total of minutes spent waiting, with one point per collection day.
data.chart3_finding: Add up every wait recorded and it comes to {{stat:wait.total_minutes}} minutes of standing in a queue, spread across {{stat:coverage.span_days}} days. That is the number that makes people look up.
data.part_of_day_title: Which part of the day I covered
data.part_of_day_body: The times were not sampled at random: I stood there when I could. This table is where the coverage looks thin, and the limitations page says what that costs the study.
data.quality_body: {{stat:timing.stopwatch}} of {{stat:timing.total}} waits were measured with a stopwatch, which is {{stat:timing.measured_share}} percent of them. The rest were estimated or reported by word of mouth, and they are counted here rather than hidden.
data.walkaway_body: People gave up and left in {{stat:walked.yes}} of the {{stat:walked.known}} rows where I could tell whether they did.
data.walkaway_none: I did not note whether people gave up and left in enough rows to report a figure for it.

action.lede: Whatever the study shows, nothing changes until somebody at the counter hears about it. Everything on this page is ready to send as it stands.
action.message_title: A message you can send as it is
action.message_body: Copy this into an email, a message or a complaint form. It states the numbers and where they came from, so the reader can check them.
action.message_data:
Subject: Waiting times measured at these counters

I measured waiting times by hand over {{stat:coverage.days_distinct}} days ({{stat:coverage.date_range}}). {{stat:coverage.collected}} waits were logged at {{stat:coverage.places_with_data}} places, and {{stat:wait.count}} of them were timed with a stopwatch.

The median wait was {{stat:wait.median}} minutes. The slowest wait was {{stat:wait.max}} minutes, and {{stat:wait.over_threshold}} waits were longer than {{stat:wait.threshold}} minutes.

Could the busiest part of the day be looked at first? The full rows, the photos and the method note are available on request.

Thank you.
action.message_partial:
Subject: Waiting times measured at these counters

I have started measuring waiting times by hand: {{stat:coverage.collected}} of a planned {{stat:coverage.target}} waits are logged so far, at {{stat:coverage.places_with_data}} places, over {{stat:coverage.days_distinct}} days ({{stat:coverage.date_range}}). The timed waits will be published here as they are recorded.

It would help to know whether waiting times are already being measured anywhere, and what the counter is expected to keep to.

Thank you.
action.message_empty:
Subject: Waiting times at this counter are not being measured

I am starting a hand-collected study of waiting times at this counter, because nothing about the queue is currently written down: not the length, not the waiting time, not how many people give up and leave.

The plan is to record {{stat:coverage.target}} waits by hand, publish the raw rows and the photos, and report what the numbers can and cannot show.

If a target or a standard for waiting time already exists, I would like to quote it correctly.

Thank you.
action.email_subject: Waiting times measured by hand at these counters
action.copy_note: Copies the text above. If that does not work, select the text and copy it yourself.
action.email_button: Open this in your email app
action.no_contact: No contact address is set in src/site.json yet, so this page cannot address the message for you. Add one and rebuild.
action.form_body: If you saw the same thing, this form turns your account into an email. It opens your own email app: this website has no server and stores nothing.
action.form_disabled: The report form appears as soon as a contact address is set in src/site.json.
action.hint_name: So the person reading it knows who is writing.
action.hint_contact: Only fill this in if you are happy to be contacted about it.
action.hint_place: For example: the counter at the main entrance, around midday.
action.hint_when: A date, or the words most days last week.
action.hint_what: How the queue was behaving, how long you waited, whether people left.
action.form_submit: Open this in my email app
action.form_note: This button hands your text to your own email program. If nothing opens, copy the message above instead.
action.print_title: Or print it and hand it over
action.print_body: The one-page summary is laid out for A4 paper: the finding, the numbers, the places and the limits of the study.
action.include_title: What to include when you report it
include_points: The place, and the hour at which you saw the queue at its worst.
How long you waited yourself, in minutes. A rough count is far more useful than none.
Whether you saw anybody give up and leave.
The date, so the report can be matched to a row in data/observations.csv.
action.privacy_note: Nothing typed on this page leaves your computer until you press send in your own email program. This site has no server of its own and keeps no data about visitors.

summary.kicker: One-page summary, ready to print or send
summary.where: Measured by hand, in person, at the places listed below.
summary.chart_caption: Every wait recorded, in five-minute buckets, with the median marked.
summary.limits_title: What this study does not prove
ask_points: Staff the busiest part of the day for the counter, instead of spreading the same hours evenly across it.
Put the usual serving time on a sign, so people can decide before they commit to the queue.
Measure it again after the change, with this same method, and publish the new numbers next to the old ones.
summary.provenance: Generated from data/observations.csv — {{stat:coverage.collected}} rows logged, data snapshot {{meta:data_hash_short}}, built {{meta:built_date}}.
summary.empty_body: The summary writes itself once observations exist. Right now it states the target and nothing else: {{stat:coverage.collected}} of {{stat:coverage.target}} rows.

limitations.lede: This section is part of the study rather than a sentence bolted on at the end. Everything below is produced by the build from the same rows as the charts, so it changes when the data changes.
limitations.about_title: What that means for these numbers
limitations.missing_body: Those columns are optional in data/observations.csv. Blanks are counted here rather than quietly filled in.
limitations.timing_caption: How each timed wait was measured
limitations.strengthen_title: What would make this study stronger
strengthen_points: More observations at the places that have fewer than {{stat:min_place_n}} timed waits, so their medians stop being indicative only.
The same places measured at the same hours on the same weekdays, so a comparison holds the day of the week still.
A second person counting alongside me, so a mistake in my own timing shows up as a difference instead of staying invisible.
A count of the people who walk past, see the queue and leave without ever joining it.
limitations.method_link: The method, the problems I ran into and the changes I made are written up in docs/method-note.md.
limitations.field_walked_away: whether anybody gave up and left
limitations.finding_not_enough_yet: Only {{finding:collected}} of the target {{finding:target}} observations are logged, so {{finding:remaining}} more rows are still needed before the figures settle down.
limitations.finding_self_selected_times: I decided when to stand in the queue. Quiet hours and quiet days are certainly under-represented, so this is not a random sample of all waiting times.
limitations.finding_single_observer_watch: Every row was collected by one person watching one queue at a time, so two slow counters at once could not both be counted.
limitations.finding_one_observer: One person, {{finding:observer}}, collected every row, and there is no second counter to check the timing against.
limitations.finding_observer_count: {{finding:count}} people collected rows, so the timing is not perfectly consistent between them.
limitations.finding_single_day: Everything was collected on one day, {{finding:date}}, so a busy Monday and a quiet Friday would look identical in this data.
limitations.finding_few_days: The rows come from only {{finding:days}} days, which is too few to separate a bad day from a bad queue.
limitations.finding_day_gaps: The collection spans {{finding:span_days}} calendar days but only {{finding:days}} of them have rows: {{finding:gap_days}} days were skipped.
limitations.finding_no_timed_waits: {{finding:logged}} observations are logged, but not one of them has a wait time recorded, so no median can be computed yet.
limitations.finding_estimate_share: {{finding:estimates}} of {{finding:total}} waits were estimated rather than timed with a stopwatch, which is {{finding:share}} percent.
limitations.finding_no_photos_yet: {{finding:logged}} rows are logged without a single photo, so there is no visual evidence on the site yet.
limitations.finding_photo_gap: {{finding:photos}} of the target {{finding:target}} photos exist, so {{finding:remaining}} are still missing.
limitations.finding_low_n_places: These places have fewer than {{finding:min_n}} timed waits, so their medians are indicative only: {{finding:places}}.
limitations.finding_places_without_data: These places are listed but have no observations at all yet: {{finding:places}}.
limitations.finding_missing_waits: {{finding:blank}} of {{finding:total}} rows have no wait time recorded, so they count towards the coverage but never towards a median.
limitations.finding_rows_without_photo: {{finding:blank}} of {{finding:total}} rows have no photo backing them up.
limitations.finding_walkaway_unknown: In {{finding:blank}} of {{finding:total}} rows I did not note whether anybody gave up and left, so the walk-away figure is a lower bound rather than a total.
limitations.finding_single_day_part: Every observation was collected in the {{finding:part}}, so the rest of the day is simply unmeasured.
limitations.finding_partial_day_parts: The rows cover only these parts of the day: {{finding:covered}}. Any part of the day with no rows at all cannot be described.
limitations.finding_no_baseline: There is no baseline. No queue was measured before any change was made, and nothing here is compared against a standard such as {{finding:threshold}} minutes.
limitations.finding_weather_not_controlled: Weather and the academic calendar were not controlled. A rainy week or a holiday week can move a queue far more than anything the counter does.
limitations.finding_no_cause: This data shows how long people waited. It cannot show why. The bottleneck could be staffing, a till, a form, or a delivery that arrives late.
limitations.finding_cannot_generalise: The rows describe {{finding:places}} places at the hours I could be there. They say nothing about waiting times anywhere else.
